findings.reason: the requirement introduced by this revision would otherwise be unenforced, and the node could ship a plan that silently answers one of two unordered reviews.
findings.text: the Deliverable newly requires that "the refusal remains only when two covering reviews cannot be ordered", but that exception is measured by no case and by no control: an implementation that deletes the ambiguity branch outright passes all four cases (a record without a run id simply falls through to `record`, which stays the newest `read_plan_review` pick) and still satisfies all five controls, since control 3 only shows the second case depends on removing the refusal

findings.reason: a node that fixes `review_coverage` alone passes every case, leaving the per-section tie picking the oldest review, and no control (not even the "correcting only `read_plan_review`" one, which runs the other direction) would show it.
findings.text: the Deliverable requires the tie broken "in both places", but case 1 cannot reach the second: with both reviews carrying the plan's fingerprint, `review_coverage`'s whole branch returns `[newest]` (plan_review.py:1024), so `read_plan_review`'s `max(covering, key=plan_version)` (plan_review.py:1269) receives a one-element list and its tie-break is dead in the test's scenario; the tie is genuinely live only in the per-section branch, where `contributing` is built ascending and ties fall to the oldest

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `plan_review.py:1269` (`max(covering, key=plan_version)`) and `plan_review.py:1024` (`max(whole, key=plan_version)`) are exact, `crew_dispatch_commands.py:2784` is the `--review-run` refusal and the "carried by N covering reviews" refusal's branch is exactly at `:2792`, as cited, `routing.py:2717` is the `review_coverage` call cited as "near line 2720", and `reckon/mcp_crew_actions.py`'s `answer` action exists at :316 with no `review_run` key at :124 or :219.
rubric_items.done_when: two findings — the newly stated refusal exception and `read_plan_review`'s own tie-break are both named in the Deliverable but measured by no case and protected by no control.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — logs are required under the run directory and each must start with its revision and literal command and end in `EXIT=`, which is durable and re-openable.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no new symbols; the new test is named for the mechanism, carrying no plan, stage or ticket label.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — I checked all three: the root cause matches the evidence (`max` on a tie returns the first record read, and `list_plan_reviews` returns "newest last", so the tie resolves to the oldest in both cited functions), each mechanism produces its case (`review_coverage`'s whole branch returns `[newest]`, so `read_plan_review`, which builds `contributing` from it, can only return that record), and every mechanism runs on a named production caller (`routing.py:2717`/`:2721` for the gate, `crew_dispatch_commands.py:2724` for the answer verb, `mcp_crew_actions.py:316` landing on `crew_review` — the last with no `review_run` key to pass, as the Why states).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — all four changes (the two tie-breaks, the widened `--review-run`, the default-to-newest answer, the MCP parameter) serve one verdict: an answer reaches the newest review that raised the finding, and each case carries its own control.
